The HEAT toolkit addresses stakeholder engagement by guiding users through the process of consulting and including diverse stakeholders in the design process. It emphasizes the importance of engaging different stakeholders, particularly marginalized and vulnerable groups, to understand the intended and unintended consequences of AI systems. The toolkit provides instructions on how to identify relevant stakeholders and encourages meaningful and power-sensitive engagement, while also addressing potential issues like tokenism and participation-washing.

Regarding environmental sustainability, the HEAT toolkit includes a section dedicated to assessing and mitigating the environmental impact of AI systems. It introduces methods for calculating the carbon footprint of AI models and conducting Life Cycle Analyses. The toolkit promotes energy-efficient programming and encourages users to rethink their product designs with environmental considerations in mind, framing the environment as an 'unimaginable user persona' to foster more-than-human-centered design practices.
